papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, discussion and conclusion; appendix not read.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes training a restricted Boltzmann machine on a D-Wave annealer to learn a random-Fourier-feature spectral distribution for kernels.

assertions.value: The authors report that on synthetic data with d = 10, test accuracy improves from 0.818 with Gaussian RFF to 0.846 after kernel learning, a difference of +0.028.
quotes: From Table I, the test accuracy on the synthetic data d = 10 improves from 0.818 with Gaussian RFF to 0.846 after kernel learning, i.e., +0.028.

quotes: Table II shows that, for all three class pairs, the highest accuracy is achieved after kernel learning, outperforming both Gaussian RFF and RKS with IKL.
our approach achieves top or comparable accuracy to a tuned Gaussian RFF and Random Kitchen Sinks with Implicit Kernel Learning

500 RBMs with the same parameters were simultaneously embedded in subgraphs on D-Wave Advantage

we should clarify whether quantum annealers can achieve quantum speedup as sampling machines in our method.

papers.title_in_file: Preconditioning for a Variational Quantum Linear Solver
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections II-III, V (results), VI, VII.
papers.what_it_is: Applies incomplete LU preconditioning to the variational quantum linear solver and simulates the effect on required ansatz depth.

assertions.value: The authors report that, applying ILU to 10 instances of linear equations from 128 × 128 random sparse matrices, they observed a reduction in the required ansatz depth in all cases owing to preconditioning.
quotes: By applying ILU to 10 instances of linear equations given by 128 × 128 random sparse matrices, we observed a reduction in the required depth of the ansatz in all cases owing to preconditioning.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical demonstration on random instances, one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Numerical simulation only; no noisy hardware run is described in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the comparison used 10 different 128×128 random sparse matrices with ansatz circuit depth varying from 1 to 20.
quotes: for linear equations defined by 10 different 128×128 random sparse matrices, with the ansatz's circuit depth varying from 1 to 20.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the steady-state heat-diffusion equation discretized into 128 segments, the residuals were lower with preconditioning than without.
quotes: In this example, we have discretized the 1D rod into 128 segments.
The residuals are lower for the preconditioned case (red line) than for the non-preconditioned case (blue line)
assertions.certainty_reason: One example problem, one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that preconditioning might increase the entanglement needed to generate the right-hand-side state, and that choosing a preconditioner requires balancing three costs.
quotes: However, this preconditioning might increase the amount of entanglement needed to generate |b⟩.

it is necessary to consider the balance between three costs: the number of gates required to generate |b⟩, the depth of the ansatz required to obtain the solution, and the additional computational cost required for preconditioning on a classical computer.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of a limit, Section VI.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Section II, Theorem 1 and Corollary 6 region of Section III, numerical summary, Section VI.
papers.what_it_is: Analyzes QAOA optimization landscapes in state space for deep circuits, with a performance indicator and numerical local-search examples.

assertions.value: The paper proves that when the classical target function meets the conditions of Theorem 1, the objective over state space has only one local minimum, which is also global, at the state of the optimal solution.
quotes: Let f fulfill the conditions of Theorem 1. Then F admits its only local and global minimum at
the critical points of F precisely are the computational basis states and the only local and also global minimum is obtained at the state corresponding to the optimal solution to f
assertions.certainty_reason: Corollary 6 with proof, Section III.4.
assertions.reader_inference: Holds for universal generators and unlimited depth; the authors call this regime far from practical use.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical results indicate QAOA performs well only on some classes of optimization problems, and state that there will be no universal applicability of QAOA in deep circuits.
quotes: Results indicate the QAOA performs well only on some classes of optimization problems.
From the results we have seen so far, it becomes however already clear that there will be no universal applicability of QAOA in deep circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' conclusion from their own analysis and simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that they numerically simulated deep-circuit QAOA with up to 1000 layers of non-decomposed QAOA gates using a simple downhill simplex method.
quotes: numerically simulating deep-circuit QAOA (up to 1000 layers of non-decomposed QAOAgates) based on a simple downhill simplex method.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that many aspects influencing local search performance were neglected, in particular the circuit depth needed to approximate a problem's solution up to a convincing ratio.
quotes: Lastly, we have to point out that many further aspects, that influence the performance of a local search, have been neglected in this work.
This especially includes the actual circuit depth required for approximating the solution of a problem up to a convincing ratio.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own limit, Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning of Molecular Energies with Hybrid Quantum-Neural Wavefunction
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results sections, hardware section, ablation, conclusion; supplementary information not available.
papers.what_it_is: Introduces pUNN, a paired UCCD circuit plus neural network wavefunction, with simulations and a superconducting-hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors report that in noiseless simulations of molecules with 8 spatial orbitals and 16 qubits, mean absolute error decreases from 51.9 mHartree for pUCCD to 0.6 mHartree for pUNN, and pUNN's error is comparable to UCCSD at 1.9 mHartree.
quotes: we perform noiseless numerical calculations on molecular systems corresponding to 8 spatial orbitals and 16 qubits.
By comparing pUNN and pUCCD, we find that, the mean absolute error (MAE) decreases from 51.9 mHartree for pUCCD to 0.6 mHartree for pUNN.
The MAE of pUNN is comparable to the MAE of UCCSD, which is 1.9 mHartree.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a superconducting quantum computer the pUNN reaction barrier is approximately 16 kcal mol−1, higher than the experimentally reported range of 2 ∼ 10 kcal mol−1, while a noiseless pUNN model gives around 9 kcal mol−1.
quotes: the reaction barrier predicted by pUNN on the quantum circuit is approximately 16 kcal mol−1.
While this value is still higher than the experimentally reported range of 2 ∼ 10 kcal mol−1 [65]
the predicted reaction barrier is around 9 kcal mol−1, which aligns well with the FCI results and experimental observations.
assertions.certainty_reason: One hardware experiment, 4 qubits only.

assertions.value: The authors report that replacing the pUCCD circuit with a Hadamard superposition circuit, in a shot-based noise-free classical emulator, leads to a noticeable decrease in accuracy and a significant increase in energy variance.
quotes: replacing the pUCCD circuit with a Hadamard superposition leads to a noticeable decrease in accuracy, along with a significant increase in energy variance.
we perform the comparison using a shot-based classical emulator which is free of gate noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: One ablation on one molecular system.

assertions.value: The authors state that their choice of a dense MLP for the neural network is a proof-of-concept and that more efficient architectures could further optimize pUNN.
quotes: As our main contribution is the novel and unique quantum-neural hybrid framework, our choice of a dense MLP for the neural network is a proof-of-concept.
More efficient architectures, such as restricted Boltzmann machines or graph neural networks, could further optimize pUNN
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own scope.

papers.title_in_file: Quaternion-based machine learning on topological quantum systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, qCNN training and results, Section V discussions.
papers.what_it_is: Uses quaternion algebra in PCA and a quaternion convolutional network to classify topological phases of Chern insulators.

assertions.value: The authors report testing accuracies of 99.67% for the qCNN and 94.12% for the conventional CNN, and attribute the difference to the spin-vortex dataset, where the qCNN works well but the CNN does not.
quotes: After the training procedure finished, the qCNN (CNN) machine gets 99.67% (94.12%) testing accuracy.
This difference in accuracy results from the spin-vortex dataset, where the qCNN works well but CNN dose not.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper's machine is a classical network run on simulated quantum-system data; no quantum hardware is involved.

assertions.value: The authors state that the qCNN has fewer total network parameters than the CNN despite being more complex, and that one epoch takes longer for the qCNN, especially on a CPU.
quotes: Although the qCNN is more complex than the CNN, the total network parameters of the qCNN is however less than the CNN.
the time of one epoch for qCNN is longer than that of convention CNN in our task, especially utilized by CPU.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the PCA input function is not gauge invariant and that the PCA method might not be more practical than the qCNN method.
quotes: Unfortunately, the F (p) is not gauge invariant.
We remark that our PCA results looked good because the inputs were ingeniously designed and the PCA method might not be more practical than the qCNN method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own limit, Section V.

assertions.value: The authors state that the qCNN's accurate classification of uncompleted winding configurations after learning spin-vortex states is its main advantage over the conventional CNN, expected to result from the quaternion algebra.
quotes: This is the main advantage of the qCNN over the conventional CNN, which is expected to result from the quaternion algebra.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' expectation about the mechanism, not tested in isolation.

papers.title_in_file: Learning in Quantum Common-Interest Games and the Separability Problem
papers.version_note: The file name carries an earlier title (Quantum Potential Games, Replicator Dynamics and the Separability Problem); the file content is arXiv 2302.04789v3 under the title shown. Same arXiv id as the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Sections 3-5 theorem statements, Section 8; appendices and most simulations not read.
papers.what_it_is: Introduces quantum common-interest games, links their Nash equilibria to the Best Separable State problem, and analyzes quantum learning dynamics.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the Nash equilibria of a two-player quantum common-interest game with common utility function u(ρ, σ) = Tr(R(ρ ⊗ σ)) correspond to the KKT points of BSS.
quotes: The Nash equilibria of a two-player quantum common-interest game with common utility function u(ρ, σ) = Tr(R(ρ ⊗ σ)) correspond to the KKT points of BSS.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3.1 with proof, Section 3.

assertions.value: The paper proves that alternating quantum best response converges to the set of Nash equilibria in two-player quantum CIGs.
quotes: Alternating Quantum BR converges to the set of Nash equilibria in two-player quantum CIGs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 4.1 with proof, Section 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classical convergence result for linear multiplicative weights does not extend to the quantum setting, because its isolated-fixed-points assumption is vacuous in quantum games: all rank-one density matrices are fixed points of lin-MMWU.
quotes: Crucially, we find that the classical result of [32] for convergence to Nash equilibria in classical CIGs does not extend to the quantum setting.
it is vacuous in quantum games as all rank-one density matrices are fixed points of lin-MMWU (Theorem 5.1)
assertions.certainty_reason: Follows from Theorem 5.1, argued in Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that proving theoretically the experimentally observed convergence of lin-QREP to Nash equilibria is open, and that whether lin-MMWU provably converges to a rank-1 matrix for both players is an open question.
quotes: the first of which is to theoretically corroborate the experimental findings for convergence of lin-QREP to Nash equilibria.
Another intriguing open question is to what extent and under what conditions can the lin-MMWU dynamics be provably shown to converge to a rank-1 matrix for both players in quantum CIGs
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of open limits, Section 8.

papers.title_in_file: Variational quantum algorithms for machine learning: Theory and Applications (PhD thesis, Stefano Mangini)
papers.partial_detail: Summary, Chapter 6 table and method text, Chapter 8 introduction, Chapter 9 Conclusions; Chapters 2-5, 7 body and appendices not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A PhD thesis reviewing variational quantum algorithms and quantum machine learning, with original work on quantum perceptrons, an autoencoder case study, QNN entanglement and noise deconvolution.

assertions.value: The author reports that in the industrial power-plant autoencoder and classifier case study, the quantum procedures performed equally well to comparable classical counterparts and were also tested on IBM superconducting hardware, and states that a clear quantum advantage is still out of reach.
quotes: For both tasks, the quantum procedures performed equally well to comparable classical counterparts, and they were also tested on real superconducting quantum hardware provided by IBM.
While the achievement of a clear quantum advantage is still out of reach, this approach sets a milestone in the field of quantum machine learning
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical toy-model result in one thesis chapter.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 6.1 holds the numbers; they were not quoted because table text did not copy cleanly.

assertions.value: The author reports that quantum neural networks initialised with random parameters reproduce the properties of Haar random quantum states under various measures, with matrix product state simulations of up to 50 qubits and a new measure called entangling speed.
quotes: showed that they reproduce the same properties of Haar random quantum states under various measures.
Employing tensor network methods (MPS) we could simulate wide quantum circuits of up to 50 qubits, and introduced a new measure, the entangling speed
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result summarised in the conclusions.

assertions.value: The author states that noise can be eliminated by deconvolution provided the noise map is known and invertible, applied as classical post-processing of outcome statistics.
quotes: Here instead we show that noise can be eliminated by means of a deconvolution process, provided that the noise map describing the process is known and invertible.
since the transformation is not applied to the quantum system itself, but to the outcome statistics as a classical post-processing step
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states the scope of its own method, Chapter 8 introduction.

assertions.value: The author states that the field is still too immature to confidently assess when and how a useful quantum advantage will be achieved, and that efficiently loading classical data into quantum registers remains open.
quotes: Although the scientific value of near-term quantum computers is undeniable, the field is still too immature to confidently assess when and how a useful quantum advantage will be achieved.
it is worth stressing that the general problem of efficiently loading classical data into quantum registers still stands open.

papers.title_in_file: Q-fid: Quantum Circuit Fidelity Improvement with LSTM Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Section V results, related work end, Section VII; method sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Presents Q-fid, an LSTM that predicts quantum circuit fidelity, compared with Qiskit's mapomatic on simulated noise models.

assertions.value: The authors report that Q-fid's prediction RMSE against mean noisy fidelity ranges from 0.003 to 0.182 with an average of 0.0515, while mapomatic's average RMSE is 0.142.
quotes: The RMSE of Q-fid's prediction compared with the mean noisy fidelity ranges from 0.003 to 0.182 with an average of 0.0515.
On the other hand, mapomatic's fidelity estimation has an average RMSE of 0.142, with a minimum RMSE equal to 0.0424 and a maximum RMSE of 0.284.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on simulated noise.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract's up to 24.7x figure is a best single case, not the typical gap.

assertions.value: The authors state that they picked 25 circuits from QASMbench and executed them on the Qiskit Aer simulator with noise models that mimic ibm nairobi and ibmq montreal.
quotes: we picked 25 quantum circuits from the QASMbench [40] NISQ benchmark suite to demonstrate the performance of Q-fid
The circuits are executed on the Qiskit Aer simulator [42] with a noise model that mimics ibm nairobi and ibmq montreal.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own evaluation setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that under a changed noise model, Q-fid's prediction is 5.31× more accurate than mapomatic on average, with the most accurate case 42.0× better, after retraining on 100 new RB circuits.
quotes: For the new noise model, Q-fid's prediction is 5.31× more accurate than mapomatic on average, with the most accurate one being 42.0× better.
Q-fid adapts to this new noise pattern and it only takes 100 new RB circuits to retrain.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a simulated noise change.

assertions.value: The authors state that the number of circuits needed for retraining might vary across processors and that fault-tolerant qubits will likely need more sophisticated fidelity metrics.
quotes: For different processors, the number of circuits needed for retraining might vary.
In the future when fault-tolerant qubits are realized, we will likely need more sophisticated metrics to evaluate the fidelity of QC outputs
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of limits.
